text: Residents have reached out to my office with concerns about speeding along their street and requested that traffic calming measures (speed humps) be installed on the street as a method of addressing these concerns. My office polled the homes and there was strong support from the residents for making this change. I am requesting that speed humps be installed on Corley Avenue between Brookside Dr and Glenmount Park Rd

The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Waived the polling requirement under the City's Traffic Calming Policy and authorized the installation of traffic calming (speed humps) on Corley Avenue between Brookside Drive and Glenmount Park Road; and 2. Directed the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter sections of the roadway to install one speed hump on Corley Avenue between Brookside Drive and Glenmount Park Road for traffic calming purposes, generally as shown on the attached Drawing No. 421G-4024, dated May 2022, from the Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services, attached to the letter (May 26, 2022) from Councillor Brad Bradford, Ward 19, Beaches - East York.
